positions.name: BareErasureCommand
positions.frame: when a directive commands the record's own content be forgotten or removed, does its authority rest on the command's bareness rather than on argument or negotiation?
positions.why: Both expressions are terse, unhedged imperatives aimed at the same shared record — one at a named decision, one at a named migration's knowledge — with no justification, hedge, or audience-softening offered. The register, relational, and power reads all converge independently on the same pattern: unilateral command exercised through bareness itself. The tension worth holding is that both target concrete past referents (per the temporal read) yet demand an irrealis erasure of them — the set holds that tension rather than resolving it, since neither referent resolves to any known node in the graph.
